- U3: Job DSL as an option for XD users to orchestrate jobs
- U4: Port field-value-counter module from XD to s-c-s repo as sink
- U5: Port aggregate-counter module from XD to s-c-s repo as sink
- U6: Port gauge module from XD to s-c-s repo as sink
- U7: Port rich-gauge module from XD to s-c-s repo as sink
- U8: Flink processor for streaming machine learning

So this is essentially the historical work of porting Spring XD modules to Spring Cloud Stream app starters (the spring-cloud-stream-app-starters repository), plus creating a Kinesis sink, plus a job DSL for composed tasks (Spring Cloud Data Flow composed tasks / DSL), plus a Flink processor.

Modules to port:
- Log sink (simple)
- Field-value-counter sink (moderate - needs Redis store)
- Aggregate-counter sink (moderate - Redis)
- Gauge sink (simple-moderate - Redis)
- Rich-gauge sink (moderate - Redis)
- Kinesis sink (new module, AWS Kinesis integration - moderate to complex)
- Job DSL (composed task DSL - this is significant work, parser, graph, execution)
- Flink processor (integration with Apache Flink, ML abstractions)

Let me structure the WBS:

Common/infrastructure activities:
1. Project setup: create module scaffolding, Maven build, parent POM alignment with s-c-s conventions, binder abstraction
2. Common design: convert XD modules (which used XD's message bus and annotations) to Spring Cloud Stream @EnableBinding model, configuration properties via @ConfigurationProperties, Spring Boot auto-configuration

Per-module activities (each includes: porting code, adapting to s-c-s model, unit tests, integration tests, docs):

- Estimate: ~10-15 days

U2: Log sink
- Simple port: LogSinkHandler with log levels, expression for message, tests, docs
- Estimate: ~3-5 days

U3: Job DSL
- This is the biggest item: DSL parser (grammar), validation, graph model, UI integration hooks, execution via composed task runner (in Spring Cloud Data Flow), tests, docs
- Historical note: this became the composed task feature in SCDF with the DSL parser in spring-cloud-dataflow (ComposedTaskRunner, TaskDefinition DSL parsing, graph)
- Estimate: ~30-40 days

U4: field-value-counter sink
- Port from XD: uses Redis (field value counter store), configuration, tests with embedded Redis, docs
- Estimate: ~5 days

U5: aggregate-counter sink
- Port: aggregate counter service, Redis store, tests, docs
- Estimate: ~5 days

U6: gauge sink
- Port: gauge service, Redis store, tests, docs
- Estimate: ~4 days

U7: rich-gauge sink
- Port: rich gauge (stores value, min, max, mean, count), tests, docs
- Estimate: ~5 days

U8: Flink processor
- New module: integrate Flink runtime within s-c-s processor, flink streaming job bootstrap, ML abstractions (flink-ml), packaging, tests, docs
- Estimate: ~12-15 days

- Release engineering: BOM updates, app starter generation, metadata (configuration properties whitelisting), CI builds
- Overall integration testing, documentation aggregation

Each module is delivered as a reusable auto-configuration library plus a thin executable app-starter application, following spring-cloud-stream-app-starters conventions, with all options externalized via @ConfigurationProperties and configuration metadata generation.
Spring XD-specific infrastructure (XD message bus, XD module annotations, XD deployment descriptors) is removed and replaced with standard Spring Cloud Stream binder configuration.

field-value-counter, aggregate-counter, gauge, and rich-gauge sinks keep their XD semantics and use Redis as the backing store via Spring Data Redis; integration tests run against Redis via Testcontainers.

The Kinesis sink is a new implementation on AWS SDK for Java v2 (KinesisAsyncClient) with record batching, configurable retries, partition-key expression support, and standard AWS credential provider chain; integration tests use LocalStack via Testcontainers.

The Flink processor embeds an Apache Flink streaming job (StreamExecutionEnvironment) bridged to Spring Cloud Stream input/output via function composition, exposing flink-ml machine learning abstractions; checkpointing and parallelism are externally configurable.

The job DSL is implemented as a standalone parser library (hand-written recursive-descent parser producing an AST) supporting sequencing, transitions/branching, and parallel composition; the AST is consumed by a composed task runner integrated with Spring Cloud Data Flow to orchestrate job execution; visualization support is limited to exposing a graph model, not building a new UI.
Testing strategy: JUnit 5, AssertJ, Spring Cloud Stream test binder for unit/integration tests, Testcontainers for Redis and LocalStack, plus end-to-end validation against RabbitMQ and Kafka binders.
Build: Maven multi-module project aligned with the existing s-c-s app-starters parent POM, apps packaged as Spring Boot fat jars, BOM and dependency management updated, CI pipeline configured.
assumptions: 's-c-s' means Spring Cloud Stream (app starters repository) and 'XD' means the legacy Spring XD project; the XD module source code (log, field-value-counter, aggregate-counter, gauge, rich-gauge) is available for porting under a compatible Apache 2.0 license.
A single developer (myself) performs all work; all estimates are person-effort in workdays (1 workday = 8 productive hours), not elapsed calendar time.
Redis is available as the metrics/counter store and a container-capable test environment (Docker/Testcontainers) is available for Redis and LocalStack.
AWS credentials/LocalStack are available for Kinesis development and testing; no production AWS provisioning, IAM setup, or cost management is included.
A Flink version compatible with Java 17 is used; scope is limited to wiring existing flink-ml abstractions into the processor - no new ML algorithms are implemented.
The job DSL covers job/task composition (sequences, transitions, parallel splits) and is integrated with Spring Cloud Data Flow's composed task execution; no graphical DSL editor is built.
Each module includes unit tests, binder-based integration tests, and reference documentation as part of its estimate.
Production deployment, performance/load testing, security hardening, and multi-release maintenance are out of scope.
Existing s-c-s repository conventions, parent POMs, and CI infrastructure can be reused with only incremental configuration.

activities.activity_description: Create/align Maven multi-module structure for the new app starters (parent POM, dependency management, BOM updates), configure CI build, and set up shared build plugins and code quality checks.

activities.activity_name: XD-to-s-c-s porting blueprint and shared test utilities
activities.activity_description: Analyze the XD modules to port, define the conversion pattern (XD bus/annotations to Spring Cloud Stream functional model with @ConfigurationProperties), and implement shared test utilities (test binder harness, embedded store helpers) reused by all ported modules.

Port the XD log sink to s-c-s: Consumer implementation with configurable log level, logger name, and SpEL expression for the logged message; unit and binder integration tests; reference documentation.

Port the XD field-value-counter sink: field name expression extraction, Redis-backed field value counter store/service auto-configuration, configuration properties, unit tests, integration tests against Redis (Testcontainers), and documentation.
Port the XD aggregate-counter sink: aggregate counter service with Redis-backed store, counter name/increment expressions, configuration properties, unit and integration tests, and documentation.
Port the XD gauge sink: gauge service writing latest values to Redis, value expression support, configuration properties, unit and integration tests, and documentation.
Port the XD rich-gauge sink: rich gauge service tracking value, count, min, max, and mean in Redis, value expression support, configuration properties, unit and integration tests, and documentation.

New Kinesis sink for s-c-s: AWS SDK v2 KinesisAsyncClient producer with batching, record aggregation, configurable retries/backoff, stream/partition-key SpEL expressions, error handling, configuration properties, unit tests, LocalStack-based integration tests, and documentation.

New Flink processor: embed a Flink StreamExecutionEnvironment bridged to s-c-s input/output bindings, wire flink-ml machine learning abstractions for stream processing, externalize checkpointing/parallelism configuration, package Flink runtime dependencies, implement unit and mini-cluster integration tests, and write documentation.

activities.activity_name: U3: Job DSL grammar and language design
activities.activity_description: Define the job DSL: grammar for sequences, transitions/branching on exit status, and parallel composition; specify syntax, semantics, and error messages with representative workflow examples for XD users.

activities.activity_name: U3: Job DSL parser and AST implementation
activities.activity_description: Implement the DSL parser (tokenization, recursive-descent parsing) producing an abstract syntax tree covering sequences, transitions, and parallel splits, with robust syntax error reporting and position tracking.

activities.activity_name: U3: DSL validation and execution graph model
activities.activity_description: Implement semantic validation of parsed definitions (unknown references, unreachable branches, cycles) and a graph model derived from the AST suitable for execution planning and for rendering the workflow structure.

Integrate DSL execution with a composed task runner that interprets the AST/graph and orchestrates job launches (sequencing, transition-based branching, parallel execution, restart/resume handling) through Spring Cloud Data Flow.

activities.activity_name: U3: Job DSL tests and documentation
activities.activity_description: Comprehensive parser/validation/orchestration test suites (valid and invalid definitions, edge cases, execution scenarios) plus DSL reference documentation and usage examples.
Aggregate module reference docs, write per-module option tables, and create end-to-end sample streaming pipelines demonstrating each sink/processor and the job DSL.

activities.activity_name: End-to-end binder validation and release engineering
activities.activity_description: Validate all modules end-to-end with RabbitMQ and Kafka binders, finalize app packaging and configuration metadata, update the BOM/version matrix, and prepare the release build.
